changelog:
A recorder can be installed without a recording drive. Choose one later in Settings > Recording: one drive, or several for a new RAID 1, 5 or 6 array.
An interrupted drive setup can be retried, started over or abandoned from the same page.
A USB drive can be used as a single recording drive.
Factory reset works with no recording drive connected, and the old drive is never written again, even if it's plugged back in.
If every drive of a RAID array is unplugged and plugged back in, recording resumes without a reboot.
A failed drive in the recording array can be replaced from Settings > Recording, and a blank drive kept as a hot spare.
Every recording drive's SMART health is checked hourly, and a drive that starts failing raises an alert before it stops recording.
A camera's codec, resolution, frame rate and bitrate can be changed from the new Video encoding card in its device drawer.
A camera that delivers video too slowly now shows as Degraded, so you know to check the camera and its network.
The camera time sync no longer switches NTP cameras to manual time, and syncs each DVR once, on its own ONVIF port.
Live view keeps working after the recorder's LAN address changes.
Camera passwords no longer appear in the recorder's console logs.
Search engines no longer index the recorder's or the Site Manager's pages.
The Site Manager covers up to 20 recorders per account, the 30-day trial covers one recorder, and the multi-site live wall is free.
Site Manager accounts can have a profile picture.
